criteria.check: src/cma/firm.py:66 defaults the lock on. src/cma/cli.py:79-86 reads it once before building the client, src/cma/graph.py:263-278 records the dispatch value, and src/cma/mcp_server.py:40-78 gates startup and ASGI creation. The hosted API accepts an unchecked authorization override at src/cma/llm.py:98-110, and the CLI graph invocation at src/cma/cli.py:92 can send remote traces under the lock.

src/cma/graph.py:175-225 and :331-338 limit the case-derived prompt to the placeholder, date-only period, metric and rule tables with the overall outcome as a row, and allowlisted redraft IDs. src/cma/metrics.py:295-299 omits evidence IDs. src/cma/policy.py:83-113 builds rule detail from computed metrics, numeric thresholds and fixed outcome text.

invariants-5.log confirms the initial and redraft sentinel cases, all five custom ID cases and the hosted CLI custom-policy case ran and passed. src/cma/graph.py:191-209 masks custom rule text and IDs outside the shipped allowlist and applies that allowlist to redraft feedback.

invariants-5.log confirms the graph-input override cases, sequential graph reuse, 503 retry checks, MCP entry points and real HTTP bind-spy cases. src/cma/llm.py:92-110 and :131-135 still let a direct hosted caller authorize construction or dispatch without a current firm configuration reading.

findings.claim: The public hosted API trusts caller-supplied authorization. Direct dispatch accepts a bare boolean, and both constructors accept an unlocked configuration object without checking whether it came from the current run.
findings.repro: With a fake SDK that counts client creation and requests, save a configuration reading while unlocked and then enable the lock. Start a new operation using the saved reading with get_llm. It constructs a client. On an existing client, a direct complete call with offline_lock=False reaches the SDK under the same locked file. The graph-input tests exercise neither public argument.

findings.claim: The offline CLI can still export LangGraph traces. The lock gates the hosted model and MCP but leaves the graph's environment-driven LangSmith callback enabled, including for graph nodes that process statement data.
findings.repro: Use a synthetic statement, the default offline lock, and the fake model. Enable LangSmith tracing with a dummy API key and point its endpoint at a recording test server. The installed LangGraph starts chain callbacks at pregel/main.py:2884 and :2919, and the installed LangChain callback manager attaches the remote tracer when tracing is enabled. The graph invocation attempts trace HTTP independently of hosted model dispatch.

findings.claim: The producer's claim that every SDK HTTP request passes its own lock check is false for redirects. Both installed SDKs follow redirects by default. Disabling retries leaves redirect handling enabled.
findings.repro: Under an unlocked configuration, direct a hosted adapter to a synthetic endpoint that responds with a 307 and a same-origin Location. Its default transport sends the redirected request after a single HostedLLM.complete check. The passing tests at tests/test_firm.py:544-563 return 503 using an injected client and only prove retry behavior.

findings.claim: The producer's API compatibility claim omits the removal of both standalone ASGI factories when the lock is off. Existing embedders now fail at app construction.
findings.repro: Set offline_lock to false and use the previously available server.sse_app() or server.streamable_http_app() to mount the app in an external ASGI host. Both raise NoASGIApp. invariants-5.log confirms the unconditional refusal, while contracts-4.log covers only SDK-owned runners.

findings.claim: The producer's compatibility claim also omits a Monzo input contract change for previously accepted transaction IDs.
findings.repro: Convert an otherwise valid booked GBP Monzo export whose Transaction ID is -tx. The previous pattern accepted that ID and the new pattern refuses it. The contract tests cover IDs starting with a dot or colon.

findings.claim: The claimed CLI exit code 4 for a failed hosted request is not_proven by a runner test. The cited SDK test calls the adapter directly and never asserts a CLI exit code.
findings.repro: Add a CLI test that lets the unlocked client construct, returns a synthetic 503 at dispatch, and asserts exit 4. Run python -m pytest -v tests/test_firm.py -k cli_hosted_failure_exits_4 after adding that test.

findings.claim: The claimed absence of a performance regression is not_proven. The runner's whole-suite duration has no baseline and does not isolate the added policy load.
findings.repro: Compare the same prompt-build and redraft workload before and after the change on the same environment. The reported pytest command only measures aggregate suite time.
